conversation.message: Hi there! It's lovely to chat with you today. How have you been doing generally lately? Anything been bringing you joy or keeping you busy?
Just trying to get through the days, to be honest. Work is a grind, and I'm just trying to keep up. I don't have time for hobbies or anything like that. Just getting to the weekend is the goal.

That sounds really demanding – work taking up all your energy like that. It’s understandable you’re just focused on getting to the weekend. When things get busy like that, do you still find yourself enjoying things you used to, or does it feel like things just… lose their color a bit?
It feels like I just turned the color down. I used to love playing guitar, but I haven't picked it up in weeks. I just don't have the energy to make the notes sound good anymore.

That makes sense – when you’re feeling drained, even things you love can feel like too much effort. You mentioned not having the energy to play guitar, and just generally feeling like things have lost their color… how would you describe your mood most days lately? And has that been a recent change, or something you’ve been feeling for a while?
It’s just... flat. I wake up, go to work, come home, watch TV, go to bed. There’s no up or down, just this... nothing. I used to get excited for things, but now it’s just routine.

It sounds like things feel very monotonous right now, just going through the motions. That “flat” feeling can be really draining in itself. I’m wondering, have you noticed any changes in your sleep or appetite lately, with everything feeling so routine?

I sleep too much. I lie in bed for hours just staring at the ceiling, and then I wake up feeling like I haven't slept at all. And food... I don't have the energy to cook, so I just order takeout or skip it.

It sounds like you're caught in a really tough cycle with sleep and food – getting too much but not feeling rested, and not having the energy to properly nourish yourself. When you're facing a lot of decisions at work, or even small ones throughout the day, do you find it easy to make up your mind, or has that become more difficult lately?
It’s like my brain is just foggy. I stare at the spreadsheet and I just can’t decide what to do. It takes me hours to make a decision that used to take five minutes.

That sounds incredibly frustrating – feeling like your thoughts are just stuck in the fog. It’s completely understandable that decisions, even small ones, would feel overwhelming when you’re experiencing that. When you find yourself struggling with those decisions, do you tend to be hard on yourself about it, or are you able to be a bit more patient with the process?
I’m hard on myself. I know I used to be able to handle it, so I tell myself I’m just lazy or getting old. It’s not fair, but I don't know how to stop being like that.

That’s a really honest thing to share – it sounds like you hold yourself to a high standard, and it’s tough when you feel like you’re not meeting it. When you’re being critical of yourself like that, do you find those thoughts tend to focus on things you’ve done, or more on who you are as a person?

It’s both. I think, ‘I used to be better than this. I used to be the one with the answers, and now I’m just lost.’ It’s like I’m looking at someone else, and I don't know how to get back to being that person.

That sounds incredibly painful – feeling disconnected from who you used to be and being so critical of that shift. It takes a lot of courage to admit that. I’m wondering, alongside feeling lost and critical, have you found yourself feeling more easily moved to tears lately, or perhaps feeling more agitated or restless than usual?
Yeah. I get frustrated, but it's not anger. It's... sadness, I guess. Just feeling sorry for myself that I got this way.

It sounds like that sadness is really weighing on you, and it’s understandable to feel sorry for yourself when you’re going through such a difficult time. When you find yourself feeling that sadness, does it come in waves, or is it more of a constant presence throughout the day?
It's constant. I wake up with it, I go to bed with it. It’s just... there.

That sounds incredibly heavy to carry with you all day – that constant feeling of sadness. It takes a lot of strength to keep going when that’s present. You mentioned feeling frustrated too, but describing it as sadness rather than anger… has that feeling of sadness ever brought you to tears, or made you feel particularly overwhelmed?
Yeah. I cried in the shower last week. I just couldn't hold it in anymore. It felt... dirty, like I was giving in.

That sounds incredibly difficult – to feel like you can’t even allow yourself to feel those emotions without feeling like you’re “giving in.” It takes a lot to reach that point. When you’re being so hard on yourself, do you ever find yourself dwelling on things you feel you *should* have done differently, or things you regret?
Yeah. I replay all the mistakes I made, like I could have done things differently. It’s pointless, but I do it anyway.

It’s really common to get stuck replaying past events, especially when you’re feeling down. It sounds exhausting to keep revisiting those “what ifs.” When you’re caught in those thoughts, do you find yourself feeling particularly guilty or blaming yourself for things?
I tell myself I’m stupid for letting it happen. I beat myself up over it.

That sounds incredibly painful – constantly replaying mistakes and being so hard on yourself. It takes a lot of energy to carry that kind of self-criticism. I’m wondering, generally speaking, do you tend to look at the future with a sense of hopefulness, or do things feel a bit… bleak right now?
I don't look ahead. I just exist. I don't see a future, I just see the next day.

That feeling of just existing, of not seeing a future… that sounds incredibly isolating. It takes a lot to keep going when things feel that uncertain. You mentioned feeling frustrated and sad, and even crying last week – have you noticed yourself feeling more easily agitated or restless alongside those feelings, or is it mostly just this heavy sadness?
It's all mixed together. I'm tired, I'm frustrated, I'm sad. It's just... everything feels heavy.

That sounds incredibly overwhelming – to have so many difficult feelings all mixed together, and everything just feeling heavy. It takes a lot of strength to describe that. I’m wondering, has your appetite been affected by all of this, or have you noticed any changes in how much you eat?
I barely eat. I just don't have the energy to cook or even order takeout.

It sounds like you’re carrying a tremendous weight right now, with everything feeling so heavy and impacting even basic things like eating. Thank you so much for sharing all of this with me today – it takes real courage to be so open, and I truly appreciate you taking the time to talk. I’m going to wrap things up here, and I hope you’re able to find some small moments of peace in the days ahead.
